question: Should OpenClaw adopt `registerReadinessCriterion`, operator-selected readiness configuration, and the four named hosting profiles as supported core and Plugin SDK contracts?
rationale: This is a product and compatibility decision: the branch establishes durable external Plugin SDK APIs and readiness semantics that deployment hosts can depend on, while the foundation PRs remain open.

options.title: Approve the readiness contract and profiles
options.body: Accept the public Plugin SDK and operator-facing readiness contract, then land the stack only with current-head deployment and upgrade proof.

options.title: Land a narrower internal-only direction
options.body: Keep readiness observations core-owned and defer public plugin registration or named profiles until their permanent contract is approved.

options.title: Defer the program
options.body: Retain existing readiness behavior and revisit the feature after a maintainer-defined deployment-contract proposal.

recommendation.title: Land a narrower internal-only direction
recommendation.body: Keep readiness observations core-owned and defer public plugin registration or named profiles until their permanent contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the supplied implementation history and can respond to scope questions, although final product acceptance requires repository owner judgment.
